To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a collagen–HA nanocomposite can be successfully prepared and electrospun into a fibrous web.

the collagen nanofibers containing HA nanocrystallites were fabricated by electrospinning of the collagen–HA co-precipitate solution and that the nanofibers supported the growth of osteoblastic cells.
a collagen–HA nanocomposite was successfully electrospun to produce a nanofibous web, and the web exhibited a high potential for bone regeneration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of electrospun nanofibrous collagen–HA nanocomposite web for bone regeneration.
the development of electrospun nanofibers for bone tissue engineering.
the fabrication of collagen–apatitic nanocomposite nanofibrous webs by electrospinning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collagen–HA co-precipitate can be electrospun into a nanofiber, and that the electrospun collagen–HA nanocomposite is a promising biomaterial for bone tissue engineering.
a nanofibers with a diameter of about 100–500 nm can be produced from a co-precipitate of collagen–HA.
electrospun collagen nanofiber containing apatite nanocrytalline is a promising candidate for bone tissue engineering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrospinning is a promising method to produce collagen–apatite nanofiber with high HA content.
the collagen–HA co-precipitation process is an effective method for producing collagen-based nanofibrous materials with high HA content.
the collagen–HA co-precipitation method is a facile way to prepare a nanofibers with HA incorporated within collagen matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrospinning technique is a facile tool to prepare collagen–HA nanocomposites into a nanofiber structure.
electrospinning of co-precipitates is a promising approach for the fabrication of nanofibers containing bioceramic particles, which are otherwise hard to electrospin.
the electrospun nanofibrous collagen–HA composite may be a promising candidate as a bone tissue engineering scaffold.
